title: Representation Learning with Quantum Signal Processing
abstract: Representation learning begins when training changes the features that define similarity between data. A frozen-kernel model only reweights a fixed geometry. We establish quantum signal processing (QSP) as a solvable quantum model of the representation-learning regime. At arbitrary depth, we compute the exact mean and variance of its quantum neural tangent kernel, revealing an input-dependent angular geometry whose diagonal remains non-self-averaging even when the underlying unitary approaches Haar randomness. We also prove a sparse-data guarantee for the full nonlinear gradient flow without freezing or ensemble-averaging the kernel: the realized dynamics converges to an integrable scalar flow with a time-dependent kernel closure and explicit convergence times. A finite-depth speed limit holds for every data set and trajectory. At higher data density, numerical results show coupled evolution beyond both the scalar and frozen-kernel descriptions. These results give a controlled theory of learned quantum data geometry with provable training dynamics beyond the frozen limit.
summary: This work develops a rigorous theory for representation learning using Quantum Signal Processing (QSP) as the model. It analyzes the evolution of the quantum data geometry, proving that the dynamics simplify to integrable scalar flows in sparse data regimes but become complex and coupled in dense regimes. This provides a controlled, first-principles understanding of quantum machine learning dynamics.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish a controlled, first-principles theory for how quantum data geometry is learned during training, moving beyond the limitations of simple frozen-kernel models.
main_result: It proves that for sparse data, the full nonlinear QSP gradient flow converges to independent, integrable scalar equations, while in the dense regime, the dynamics become coupled and deviate from simpler predictions.
method: The authors use rigorous mathematical analysis, including calculating exact means and variances of the Quantum Neural Tangent Kernel (QNTK) and deriving convergence bounds using techniques like Gronwall's inequality.
model_or_system: The core model is Quantum Signal Processing (QSP), which is used as a solvable quantum model for representation learning. The dynamics are governed by the gradient flow of a loss function, leading to the evolution of the QNTK.
key_observables: The Quantum Neural Tangent Kernel (QNTK), the loss function $L(t)$, and the convergence error $\epsilon_T$ are key observables.
important_parameters: Depth ($d$), sample density ($n$), and the ratio $w = n/\sqrt{d}$ define the different learning regimes (sparse vs. dense).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes specific scaling conditions (e.g., $n^{3/2}[1 + \log n] / \sqrt{M} 	o 0$ for the sparse limit) and relies on the QSP model being an adequate representation of the learning process.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the convergence of the normalized diagonal QNTK to a Beta distribution and show the QSP training trajectory deviating from scalar or frozen-kernel predictions in the dense data regime.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the QSP model, calculating kernel statistics in the large-depth limit, then deriving convergence guarantees for the full nonlinear gradient flow, and finally comparing the full dynamics against simplified scalar and frozen-kernel approximations across sparse and dense regimes.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical treatment of learning dynamics using quantum resources provides a powerful theoretical framework for understanding how quantum information processing can model complex, non-linear machine learning phenomena.
